title: FORMAT with "MMMM" (upper case) gives the full month name: January

source.supports: the TMDL of the hidden table Power BI's auto date/time creates: its Month column is FORMAT([Date], "MMMM")

source.quote: Each table also includes six calculated columns: Day, MonthNo, Month, QuarterNo, Quarter, and Year.
source.supports: the screenshot of the table's rows shows Month = January for 01/01/2019

derivation: Two published sources joined: SQLBI prints the auto date/time table's Month column as FORMAT([Date], "MMMM"), and Microsoft Learn shows that column as January on the row for 01/01/2019. So FORMAT ( DATE ( 2019, 1, 1 ), "MMMM" ) is "January". Not `published`, since no one page shows the formula with its output, and Learn says the rows "would look similar to" its example.
